_doc: A PLANTING RECORD for the 1812 scene (T-2497): the Kinzie house's poplar row and the two cottonwoods behind it, read by renderers/web/js/trees.js through data/flora/index.json and scoped there to scene 1812, so they stand in no other year. Zone z10_settled_town is named because it is the record that describes both species as planted and grown trees; the Kinzie establishment is the one settled ground on the north bank in 1812.
name: The Kinzie house's four Lombardy poplars and two cottonwoods

existence.note: THE POPLARS: Currey (1912, ch. II) has John Kinzie plant 'four Lombardy poplars at the foot of the slope on which the house stood' after he bought the house in 1804; Wau-Bun describes them standing in 1831. Nothing dates the planting before August 1812, so their standing in this scene is inferred from a planting after 1804 and a row still standing in 1831, and from Lossing's view, which draws them against the first fort. THE COTTONWOODS: Wau-Bun, describing 1831, 'Two immense cottonwood-trees stood in the rear of the building'; trees immense in 1831 stood in 1812.

stems.note: STEM 1 OF 4 IN THE KINZIE POPLAR ROW. Currey: Kinzie 'planted four Lombardy poplars at the foot of the slope on which the house stood'; Wau-Bun, of 1831: the green 'shaded by a row of Lombardy poplars'. The 1857 engraving stands the four along the green's river-side fence, the first opposite the house's east half and the rest beyond its east end, and Lossing's row recedes east along the same line; so the row stands 1.2 m inside the south side of kinzie_house_1812_green, at the foot of the bank's rise. 4.5 m between stems is this record's own. HEIGHT 12 m is the floor of the species' 12-18 m band in z10_settled_town: about eight seasons from a planting after the fall of 1804 would give less, and Lossing's view draws them two to three times the house's height, so the band's floor is held rather than gone under.

ONE OF THE TWO COTTONWOODS BEHIND THE HOUSE. Wau-Bun, of 1831: 'Two immense cottonwood-trees stood in the rear of the building, one of which still remains as an ancient landmark'; data/exclusions.json kinzie_house adds that they are 'separately attested and one survived into the 20th century'. Every picture draws a great broad crown behind the house. Where each stood is this record's own: behind the house, toward either end. Moved 3.5 m north at T-2485 (from N +349.0), when the bake-house the pictures draw behind the house's west end took the ground just behind it; the renderer keeps a stem 4.5 m clear of every footprint. HEIGHT 21 m, inside the species' 18-26 m band in z10_settled_town: trees 'immense' in 1831 were already grown in 1812.

research_note: WHAT WOULD MOVE THESE. A measured plan of the Kinzie lot, or the Sarony lithograph after Mrs. John H. Kinzie's sketch (Currey's plate facing p. 32, not yet in the image store, T-2498), would place the row and the two trees. Until then their places are reconstructed (docs/LIBERTIES.md L-kinzie-house-1812-2497). T-3106: in_structure names the green's own fence footprint, where the four poplars are explicitly planted; the two rear cottonwoods remain outside it. This existing planted-container rule exempts only that polygon, never the house, other walls or travelled tracks. No stem or source claim moves.
